questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-7y=0 \\ -3x+6y=2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -7 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -7 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 6-(-7)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}6 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}6 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}6 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=1 \\ 8x+3y=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 3-(-2)\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{31}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{31}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -8 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+2y=1 \\ 2x-3y=-2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot (-3)-2\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}7x-y=0 \\ x+4y=1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{7\cdot 4-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{29}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{29}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+3y=5 \\ x+4y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot 4-1\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{11}[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{11}[\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-x=3y \\ y=-x+1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-x-3y=0 \\ x+y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot 1-(-3)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find a solution to the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+y=2 \\ 4x+3y=6.\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14080115/assets/843dcd4359e4b61eb9715966fbbe6c26363ab5cfc57c55f94b6a41a73ec7feb1.png)

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14080115/assets/b9ba240f93ee3ec8c02e9718d62342dca0e0855e24c7b34ed97758a6eb7c46b8.png) This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2-4\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the solution is $x=0$ and $y=2.$

{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ 6y-5x=-8.\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ -5x+6y=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $A\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14080115/assets/240a1d2f7f93ec808127c9fa1791a77a43fcd7c0c84505540acc81c8b9fbc6e1.png)

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14080115/assets/7850cbafc78f2cf2ce14ae7111064bf2f5a029f4d1b97b6d5ebfc09e7126f44e.png) This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6\cdot 2-3\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=-3.$
